title: Rasputin
anecdote: Can the shadow of destiny stretch so far that a disco star ends his life mathematically mirroring the death of the monk he sang of? During the freezing years of the Iron Curtain, Boney M crossed into Moscow under strict censorship, banned from singing their anthem of rebellion. To the communist regime, the song was an insult; yet on snowy streets, the youth embraced it through clandestinely traded cassette tapes. A year later in Poland, the group defied authority before millions, unleashing pure euphoria with those forbidden chords. On stage, the charismatic Bobby Farrell embodied the wild, mystical figure of Rasputin, fusing his own soul with the myth. Until one cold December night, death claimed him in a hotel room in Saint Petersburg during a winter tour. He died on the exact same day, and in the same city, where the monk was assassinated a century before. A haunting, eternal echo that music could never silence.
